title: Baki Hanma's struggle with depression
summary: An analytical essay on the first arc of Grappler Baki as the story of an abused child's depression. Baki was raised by a sadistic father and starved of his mother's love, which left his fighting impure and his life without meaning. A friend's support and a surrogate family help him, and he recovers only by realising that change must come from within and that he must follow his own path.
claims: Children need love, discipline, a stable environment and routine; neglect can cause lifelong mental health issues even in neurotypical people
Baki's pursuit of martial arts was impure: it was forced on him and he fought only to win his mother's love
Depression is like a bottomless pit; a friendly hand can make all the difference in climbing out and staying out
A surrogate family of friends can help you separate from blood relatives who treat you like strangers
When friends treat you well, past mistreatment becomes obvious and being yourself gets easier
The depressive mind keeps looking for external reasons for its plight; the answer is within, and if the spirit is sick the spirit must change
Blaming situational factors for internal struggles traps you in self-pity
Master the inside and the outside will change before your eyes
A fulfilling existence comes from following your own path with an exuberant, unashamed heart
